children: Shares of Hindustan Unilever Ltd. (HUL) will be in focus on Monday, September 7, after the company outlined its growth strategy and financial priorities at its Investor Day.
HUL said premiumisation, category creation and deeper distribution will drive the next leg of growth, with management remaining constructive on FY27 growth.
The company expects volume-led growth to be driven by three key levers: consumption and premiumisation, which will contribute 40% of the growth delta; market-making at 40%; and new spaces at 20%.
HUL also raised its medium-term EBITDA margin guidance range to 22-24% from 22.5-23.5% earlier, while increasing its capex intensity target to 3% of sales from 2% previously.
What brokerages said after HUL Investor Day

CLSA retained its 'Hold' rating on HUL with a price target of ₹1,804 per share. The brokerage said HUL is building a stronger growth engine around a more desirable portfolio, channel-specific execution and superior products.

It expects dedicated quick-commerce capabilities and science-led innovation to strengthen the company’s competitiveness. A 500-basis-point productivity and mix-led savings programme is also expected to provide funding for growth investments.
According to CLSA, this gives HUL room to raise capex intensity to around 3% of sales and widen its EBITDA margin guidance to 22-24%, while continuing to target competitive volume-led growth.
Jefferies retained its 'Buy' rating on HUL but cut its price target to ₹2,450. The brokerage said HUL’s playbook for 'New India' is shifting from broader reach to sharper, segment-led growth.
Management sees premiumisation, category creation and deeper distribution driving the next leg of growth, supported by AI-led execution and a large self-funded reinvestment cycle.
Jefferies said that management remains constructive on FY27 growth, while the medium-term margin guidance has been modestly widened to 22-24%.

HSBC maintained its 'Buy' rating with a price target of ₹2,440. The brokerage highlighted HUL’s volume-led growth strategy, with consumption and premiumisation accounting for 40% of the growth delta, market-making contributing 40% and new spaces accounting for the remaining 20%.
HSBC said the overall guidance remains unchanged, apart from the wider margin band, and believes clearer FY27 guidance could have helped ease investor sentiment.
The brokerage expects a performance pick-up in the coming quarters to drive the stock’s performance.
Nomura retained its 'Buy' rating with a price target of ₹2,450, saying HUL is gearing up to 'Win in New India' with its 'SASSY' approach.
However, the brokerage said that no specific FY27 guidance was provided. It said the absence of the earlier-indicated double-digit EPS growth guidance was a notable omission.
Nomura highlighted the revision in the operating margin band to 22-24% from 22.5-23.5%, while capex intensity has been raised to 3% of sales from 2% earlier.
Morgan Stanley retained its 'Equalweight' rating on HUL with a price target of ₹2,480.
The brokerage said management appeared focused on delivering volume-led growth and remained confident about its portfolio and initiatives undertaken over the past year.
It also highlighted the widening of the EBITDA margin guidance band to 22-24% from 22.5-23.5% and the increase in capex intensity to 3% of revenues from 2% earlier.

title: HUL bets on premiumisation, deeper distribution for growth, but analysts remain cautious
